newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-POLICEMEN AIM TO DERAIL LOKOMOTIV CUP RUN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-POLICEMEN AIM TO DERAIL LOKOMOTIV CUP RUN.

text.p: Lokomotiv Moscow could complete the most successful run in their history on Wednesday if they retain the Russian Cup.
But city rivals and league leaders Dynamo aim to derail Lokomotiv's two-season unbeaten cup run, their best since they won the very first Soviet Cup in 1936.

Dynamo, the police and KGB side who dominated Soviet soccer under Stalin, hope a win in the final will set them up for a first double in 60 years after decades of chronic under-achievement. They last won the league 21 years ago,

Lokomotiv, the only Moscow premier league club never to win a Soviet or Russian league title, came from behind against favourites Spartak last year to snatch the Cup 3-2, ex-Dynamo full-back Yuri Drozdov netting the 85th minute winner.
A 3-1 defeat by Spartak in their last league game should not have dented the state railway club's confidence.
The result flattered the league champions, who were lucky to survive a succession of fast breaks by international midfielders Yevgeny Kharlachev and Alexei Kosolapov.

Kosolapov, who scored twice from the spot in last year's final, had a penalty saved by the Spartak goalkeeper but will take heart from a magnificent diving header he scored in Russia's 2-0 victory over Israel in a World Cup qualifier on Sunday.
Sergei Ovchinnikov, playing one of his last games in the Lokomotiv goal before he heads for Benfica, will also be on a high after a couple of excellent saves against the Israelis.
Faced with the fast-breaking Lokomotiv attack, Dynamo can lay claim to one of the best defensive units in the league -- they have conceded only one goal in their last eight matches.
Oleg Terekhin, top scorer in the Russian league, and 23-year-old Sergei Grishin will be the main threats for Dynamo.
